pathwayLabel: Full Standard Application Required — No Reciprocity, No Abbreviated Out-of-State Path for This Classification
examName: TDLR/PSI Class A or Class B Environmental Air Conditioning exam — the same exam any first-time Texas applicant takes; no exam waiver exists outside the Georgia/South Carolina reciprocity agreements
steps: Texas TDLR's Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (ACR) Contractor reciprocity is limited to Georgia and South Carolina — confirmed directly from the ACR002 license application's own reciprocity section (§19), which requires a letter of good standing specifically from one of those two states. Florida is not eligible for reciprocity under any circumstance.

A Florida ACR/HVAC license holder instead files the standard ACR002 application — the identical form any first-time applicant uses. Texas offers no separate, abbreviated out-of-state track for this classification (unlike Texas's plumbing license, which does have one).

Document at least 48 months (4 years) of qualifying practical experience within the preceding 72 months (6 years), verified on TDLR's own Experience Verification Form by someone other than the applicant. Experience gained while holding the Florida license should count toward this, but TDLR still requires its own verification paperwork regardless of the applicant's existing license.

Alternatively, substitute qualifying education (an A/C-related associate's or bachelor's degree, or a shorter certification program) for part of the experience requirement, per the form's own education-substitution table.
Submit the $115 non-refundable TDLR application fee.

Once TDLR approves the application, schedule and pass the PSI-administered Texas licensing exam for the applicable class (Class A or B). TDLR does not publish PSI's separate exam fee in its own materials.
Obtain the required certificate of insurance before the license is issued.
notes: Confirmed by direct pdftotext extraction of TDLR Form ACR002 (rev. October 2022, still the current form as of this research) after an earlier WebFetch summary of TDLR's HTML reciprocity pages proved directionally correct but lacked this level of detail. §19 of the form states reciprocity requires 'a letter of good standing from South Carolina or Georgia which also indicates you have taken and passed an exam to obtain the out of state license' — Florida is categorically excluded, not merely absent from a list. Outside of SC/GA, every applicant — regardless of home state — files the same ACR002 application and documents the same 48-month experience requirement; there is no partial-credit mechanism for an existing out-of-state license the way Texas's plumbing board offers. The $115 fee is TDLR's own filing fee only; PSI's separate exam-scheduling fee is not published in TDLR's materials and is omitted here. Effective-version check (2026-09-29): the ACR002 PDF served at the sourceUrl today still reads 'rev October 2022'; its $115 fee, Georgia/South Carolina-only reciprocity, and 48-of-72-months experience wording were re-confirmed in that download. The $115 contractor application fee also matches 16 Tex. Admin. Code §75.80(1), most recently amended effective 9/1/2024 (49 TexReg 6449) — read via Cornell LII's mirror of the TAC, not the Secretary of State's official TAC viewer, which did not return the rule text to an automated request. Unlike Florida's F.A.C., the Texas rule does not incorporate ACR002 by revision date, so there is no official effective-date record for the form itself; that the October 2022 form is the version TDLR currently expects is inferred from it being the one TDLR's own site serves, not independently verified.
officialSourceName: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR), Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors Program
